clue.text: See rough-and-ready hospital boss met misguided WHO man

indicators.note: something misguided has gone astray, so these letters wander into a new order

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An invitation to look at a slapdash health chief who has bumped into a wrong-headed official at the World Health Organization.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misguided' shuffles SEE, ROUGHANDREADY, H, BOSS and MET, all 24 letters, into the three names. 'hospital boss' reads as one idea, but 'boss' is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus is the Ethiopian Director-General of the World Health Organization, its leading official.

clue.text: Shakespeare's age when he wrote Hamlet?

definitions.text: Shakespeare's age when he wrote Hamlet?

parts.words: Shakespeare's age when he wrote Hamlet?
parts.note: age looks like how many years old the playwright was, but it means the era: the play dates from the reign of the first Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A trivia question about how old Shakespeare was when he wrote his famous tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The solver reaches for a number of years; the answer is a historical period instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet was written around 1600, late in Queen Elizabeth I's reign, the period named after her.

clue.text: Dish Jewish leader initially put in hamper

parts.note: a rabbi leads a Jewish congregation

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to hamper is to tie, restrict movement

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word put

explanation.surface: A rabbi packs a dish into a picnic hamper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' looks like the basket, but it is the verb, giving TIE, with P pushed in after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit pie is a traditional British savoury pie, a meal served on a plate.

clue.text: Don't talk about fate or sin

indicators.note: about here means going around, so the hush wraps the next piece

parts.note: SH is the hushing sound meaning be quiet
one's lot is one's fate in life

explanation.surface: Advice not to chatter about destiny or wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth, laziness, is one of the seven deadly sins, so it is an example of a sin.

clue.text: Chance one day to cut stress

indicators.note: to cut means these pieces slice into the word for stress

parts.note: an accent is the stress put on a syllable
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Taking a day off at random to reduce one's stress levels.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is something happening by chance, as in 'by accident'.

clue.text: See 1
Rail about dissolute fellow's sentimentality at first

indicators.note: at first says the sentimentality piece goes at the front of the rest

parts.note: corn is mawkish, sentimental material
C is short for circa, about
a rake is a dissolute man about town

explanation.surface: Someone ranting against a womaniser's mushy feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' looks like the verb, to rant; it is the bird family.
explanation.definitionFit: The corncrake is a bird of the rail family, found in hayfields and meadows.

clue.text: Deity elevated old woman showing blind faith

indicators.note: elevated, in a down clue, means the word is lifted, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a deity is a god
one's old woman is one's mother, MA

explanation.surface: A god raised up by an old woman displaying unquestioning belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is doctrine accepted without question, belief held on authority alone.

clue.text: Fortune Truss keeps after taxes

indicators.note: keeps means the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: Liz Truss, the short-lived UK prime minister, holds on to a fortune once taxes are paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Net pay or profit is the amount left once deductions such as tax are taken off.

clue.text: Much ado about Republican as dystopian leader

indicators.note: about says the fuss goes around the next piece

parts.note: much ado is a big bother, a great fuss

explanation.surface: A political fuss about a Republican cast as a tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Brother is the all-seeing ruler of Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four, a nightmare future state.

clue.text: Cleans out bottle

definitions.meaning: to gut a fish is to clean out its insides
bottle is British slang for courage

explanation.surface: Washing out a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutting removes the innards; guts, like bottle, is informal for nerve or courage.

clue.text: Drive out in attempt to cross North Island

indicators.note: to cross here means the attempt straddles the following letters

parts.note: to have a bash is to have an attempt

explanation.surface: Trying to drive across the North Island of New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish someone is to expel them, sending them away from a place.

clue.text: Wanting coin? Twas ever thus

explanation.surface: A sigh about always being short of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking coins means having no small money; things staying as they always were is the same phrase, unchanged.

clue.text: See 1
Bottomless river with source in Pennines

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: a river's source is its start, so only the first letter of Pennines is used

explanation.surface: A river that seems endlessly deep, rising in the Pennine hills of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bottomless is so deep its floor cannot be found.

clue.text: Seize public land we're told, and forest creatures

indicators.note: we're told signals a word heard spoken, so a near-twin in sound is used

parts.note: a common is land open to the public
deer are animals of the forest

explanation.surface: Taking over the village green and its wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: COMMON spoken sounds like the first part of the answer, COMMAN, to which DEER is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To commandeer is to take possession of something by force or authority, especially for military use.

clue.text: Time served in rebel vessel for training

indicators.note: served in suggests the time is spent inside, so T goes within

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion against Henry VI in 1450
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: A prison term or hitch aboard a rebel ship, served as training.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led an English peasants' revolt in 1450.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadetship is the post of a cadet, someone undergoing training for the forces or police.

clue.text: Unqualified and not working properly

parts.note: a system that is down is not working
done right is done properly

explanation.surface: A worker without credentials who does the job badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unqualified' suggests lacking credentials; here it means absolute, as in a downright lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright means utter or absolute, without reservation, which is the sense of unqualified.

clue.text: Hackneyed article about studied line in music?

indicators.note: about says the article goes around the other pieces

parts.note: THE is the definite article
to read a subject is to study it
a bar line is a line in written music marking off bars

explanation.surface: A worn-out piece of writing about a melody someone has studied.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare, literally worn thin, figuratively means overused and stale.

clue.text: Certain country backed deporting one journalist

indicators.note: backed, in a down clue, means the word runs upwards, reversed
deporting means sending one piece out of the country

parts.note: Russia is a country
I is the Roman numeral one
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A country is sure to support expelling a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deporting' removes I from RUSSIA, leaving RUSSA, which 'backed' reverses to ASSUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Assured means sure or guaranteed, as certain does.

clue.text: Buckle after fighting pressure

parts.note: fighting is war
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Collapsing under stress after combat.
explanation.definitionFit: To warp is to bend or twist out of shape, as a buckled wheel does.

clue.text: Perks up when embracing chum in the Six Counties?

indicators.note: embracing means the outer word hugs the pieces inside

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
the Six Counties is a name for Northern Ireland, NI
a chum is a mate

explanation.surface: Someone cheers up hugging a friend in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Six Counties are the counties of Northern Ireland, part of the UK; 'embracing' puts the region and the chum inside the word for when.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate is to enliven, giving energy, so it perks someone up.

clue.text: Carla gutted to leave Mediterranean island, but no big deal

indicators.note: to leave means those letters depart from the island

parts.note: Minorca is a Balearic island in the Mediterranean

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Carla, devastated to leave her holiday island, is told it does not matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' reduces Carla to CA, which 'to leave' removes from MINORCA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minor is of little importance, not a big deal.

clue.text: Dogs unleashed possibly taking steamship around carrier

indicators.note: around means the ship's letters go round the carrier

parts.note: a tray carries things

explanation.surface: Loose dogs perhaps boarding a steamer with their kennel carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Strays are dogs without owners, roaming free; unleashed ones may be, hence possibly.

clue.text: Old county girl needing surgery

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally
an op is a surgical operation

explanation.surface: A woman from a historic shire needs an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: Salop is the old name for Shropshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Salop was the official name of the county of Shropshire from 1974 to 1980.

clue.text: Whisky certainly available here over bar

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: Assurance that Scotch is sold at this bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Oban is a Scottish west-coast port with its own distillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban, a Scottish harbour town, has a distillery making a single malt of the same name.

clue.text: Man-mountain?

definitions.meaning: ... is Scottish for a mountain peak, as in ... Nevis

explanation.surface: A huge, burly fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben is a boy's name and also a Scottish word for a high peak, as in Ben Nevis.

clue.text: One tends to watch crazed girl shoot, having loaded round

indicators.note: having loaded means a piece is packed inside, like a bullet in a gun
crazed means wild, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a round thing, O, is also a gun's round

explanation.surface: A deranged girl fires a loaded gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazed' scrambles the girl and shoot letters; 'having loaded' puts the round inside. 'watch' looks like observe, but is the timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A horologist makes and repairs clocks and watches, so tends them.

clue.text: Brave upstanding character died after Pinter plays

indicators.note: after places the remaining pieces behind the rearranged name
plays suggests the playwright's name is performed in a new order

parts.note: I is the letter that stands straight up

explanation.surface: A noble man dies following performances of Harold Pinter's plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' rearranges PINTER as INTREP, followed by I and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless, showing courage.

clue.text: Prize tree and fertiliser

parts.note: a pot is a trophy cup, a prize
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A prize-winning tree and what fed it.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash, a potassium compound, is widely used as fertiliser.
